name: Christianity
summary: Christianity is the religion of the historic community deriving from Jesus of Nazareth, with the Christian Bible (Old and New Testament) as its scripture. Its stated positions on politics are few and mostly come from scripture: authority is ordained by God, the faithful pay taxes and obey rulers, wealth and possessions carry duties and dangers, Christ is the only way of salvation, and marriage and sexual conduct follow creation. Churches and traditions differ widely on most political questions, so the profile is thin.
scope: The religion as the defining reference works describe it (Britannica, the Encyclopaedia Judaica entry, World History Encyclopedia, the Catholic Encyclopedia entry), answered from the Christian Bible, which they name as its sacred texts. Denominations (Catholicism, Protestantism, Orthodoxy), Christian parties and movements, and Christian-derived ideologies are other subjects and are not used. Where scripture takes no position, or churches differ and the scripture is silent, the answer is null.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Romans 13:1 states that there is no power but of God and that the powers that be are ordained of God.

universal-morality.rationale: Romans 2:14-15 says Gentiles without the law do by nature the things contained in it, the law being written in their hearts, so moral truth holds beyond one people.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Acts 4:12 and John 14:6 state that salvation and access to the Father come through Christ alone, and the Catholic Encyclopedia presents Christianity as the only absolute religion, so all religions are not expressions of one truth.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Scripture makes faith the ground (1 Corinthians 2:5: faith should stand not in the wisdom of men but in the power of God; Hebrews 11:6) and warns against leaning on one's own understanding (Proverbs 3:5).

noblesse-oblige.rationale: 1 Timothy 6:17-18 charges the rich to do good, be rich in good works and be ready to distribute.

simple-living.rationale: 1 Timothy 6:8 says that having food and raiment we should be content, and 6:9-10 warns against the desire to be rich.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: 1 Timothy 6:9-10 says those who will be rich fall into snares and hurtful lusts and that the love of money is the root of all evil; Luke 12:15 says life does not consist in abundance of possessions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: 1 Corinthians 10:24 says let no man seek his own but another's wealth, and 13:5 that charity seeketh not her own; Matthew 22:39 does presuppose love of oneself, so the rejection is of self-interest as the standard, not of self-regard.

filial-duty.rationale: 1 Timothy 5:4 tells children and grandchildren to learn piety at home and requite their parents, calling it good before God.

premarital-sex.rationale: 1 Corinthians 6:18 commands to flee fornication and Hebrews 13:4 says God will judge whoremongers and adulterers; the prohibition is not limited to one sex.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Matthew 19:4 (Jesus) states that the Creator at the beginning made them male and female, so sex is given in creation, not made by society.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: On the question 'is it lawful to put away a wife for every cause', Matthew 19:3-9 answers that divorce except for fornication is adultery, so ending a marriage without fault is rejected.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ephesians 5:22-24 says wives are to submit to their husbands in everything because the husband is the head of the wife; 1 Corinthians 7:4 gives each spouse authority over the other's body only.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: 1 Timothy 2:12 does not permit a woman to teach or have authority over a man and 3:2 requires a bishop to be the husband of one wife; the scripture also names women in service roles (Romans 16:1), so the answer is not strong.

death-penalty.rationale: Genesis 9:6 says whoever sheds man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, and Romans 13:4 says the ruler bears not the sword in vain as God's avenger on evildoers.

work-for-welfare.rationale: 2 Thessalonians 3:10 states that if any would not work, neither should he eat.

taxation-theft.rationale: Romans 13:6-7 tells believers to pay tribute and render taxes to whom they are due, because the authorities are God's ministers.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Romans 13:1-5 says to be subject to the authorities not only for wrath but for conscience sake, so lawful authority creates a moral duty, though Acts 5:29 sets obedience to God above men.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: Genesis 9:3 gives every moving thing that lives as food for man, and Genesis 1:28 gives dominion over the animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Genesis 9:3 permits eating animals, and Proverbs 12:10 says a righteous man regards the life of his beast, so humane killing for food is acceptable.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Proverbs 12:10 says a righteous man regardeth the life of his beast while the mercies of the wicked are cruel.

ban-spanking.rationale: Proverbs 13:24 says he that spareth his rod hateth his son, so scripture commends corporal discipline of children.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Matthew 6:33 says to seek first the kingdom of God, placing God, not work, at the centre of life.

notes: Themes searched: authority and obedience, tax, wealth and poverty, marriage and sex, war and violence, animals, religion and truth. Answers rest on the Christian Bible as the defining sources name it; the New Testament was preferred where the Old and New differ. Statements on which churches differ and scripture is silent, or where the record of Christian states runs against the text (revolution, religious war, restricting conversion, equality before the law), are left null. The reference works are saved copies of their pages; Britannica's saved copy is mostly its table of contents. Wikipedia was used only to find leads.
